### 702: all polynomial slices, all constant directions, and primitive division

Source: research/all-slice-projected-lnd-obstruction-pass702-working.md.
The entire643 frame is reused, not claimed as a new example:

    B=C[a,b,c,u], A=C[a,b,c], E=partial_u,
    D=a partial_b+b partial_c,
    alpha=a, beta=b-au, gamma=c-bu+a u^2/2,
    U=u+alpha gamma^2+beta gamma^3+gamma^5.

For EVERY h in A and EVERY constant ambient direction lambda,
projection at u+h=0 is locally nilpotent if and only if the
alpha,beta,gamma coefficients of lambda vanish. All surviving fields
are scalar multiples of D, fixing the line a=b=0. The proof isolates
the divergence term -(1+Dh)Q. Its factor1+Dh never vanishes identically,
and exact degrees3d+2,5d+3,7d+4 for d=deg(h)>=1 exceed the remaining
divergence terms. Constant h is a
separate invertible-linear-coordinate case with degrees2,3,4.

General then supplied a stronger uniform lemma: EVERY nonzero raw
projection is already primitive. In its only difficult case, a common
coefficient factor g divides a polynomial P in C[a,f], f=2ac-b^2,
with scalar leading f-coefficient. Also (g,a)=A. Factorial closure of
kerD=C[a,f] puts both factors of P in that ring. Specialization at
a=0 forces g(0,f) constant, while the scalar leading coefficient
prevents any positive f-degree from disappearing there. Hence g is
constant. Both the quartic eliminant and its separate cubic boundary
are printed and checked. Primitivity is not confused with the unit
coefficient ideal: D itself is primitive but has a fixed line.

Thus no polynomial slice shift, constant affine reframing, or primitive
division of these raw projections gives a free intrinsic LND. The
exact nonlinear repair T_gamma+G T_U=partial_c works before AND
after every slice projection. The base is already polynomial and
alpha is an invariant ambient coordinate; this is not nonrecognition.

The antecedents are precisely643's primitive leading fields,644's
homogeneous components and internal closure,658's complementary-basis
obstruction, and the ledger's earlier ONE-slice divergence control.
Root read643 completely in56c37e and644/658 plus that ledger subsection
in4b7279. The new project-local scope is raw projections over ALL
slices, including primitive division. No literature priority is claimed.

### 703: a nonzero common centralizer is automatically a sliced LND

Source: research/raw-projection-centralizer-slice-criterion-pass703-working.md.
For ANY principal polynomial retraction rho:C[z0,...,zn] -> A over C,
set r_i=rho(zi) and D_i=rho partial_i|A. The new conditional result is

    0!=X in Der(A), [X,D_i]=0 for all i
       implies X is locally nilpotent and has v in A with Xv=1.

No initial product B=A[s] or local nilpotence of X is assumed.
The relation module from654 gives Xe=lambda e. With b_i=Xr_i,

    D_j b_i=-e_i(Xh_j+lambda h_j).

Hence the b_i have transcendence degree at most one. In the nonconstant
case, de Bondt Corollary3.2 supplies b_i=P_i(f), with f polynomial
and in their fraction field. Retraction gives B intersect Frac(A)=A,
so f belongs to A. Dividing the derivative tuple P_i' by its gcd,
Bezout and unimodularity give e=c C(f) for c in C*. If Xf is nonzero,
Wronskians force e constant, and654 makes X a constant coordinate
translation. If Xf=0, then X^2r_i=0, which proves local nilpotence.
The all-constant-b_i case is immediate.

For the slice upgrade, I=(Xr_i) is stable under every D_j, hence under
every derivation. Smoothness rules out a proper nonzero such ideal:
in a regular local ring, a tangent derivation lowers the least positive
order of a nonzero ideal element. Thus I=A. In the Xf=0 branch,
gcd(P_i)=1 and a univariate Bezout identity supplies the explicit slice
v=sum Q_i(f)r_i. The other branches have immediate linear slices.
The note includes the entire local argument, not just a smoothness slogan.

The nonconstant-normal control has actual ambient coordinates
(a,af+u,c+af^2+2fu,f), whole inverse, and projected fields
(partial_a+f^2 partial_c,-2f partial_c,partial_c,partial_f).
X=partial_a commutes with all of them and has slice a. A graph
control rho(t)=-x^2 shows why X^2r_i=0 must NOT be stated for the
constant-normal branch: X=partial_x gives X^2r_t=-2.

Existence is genuinely missing. In702 at h=0, commuting with D and
V_alpha=partial_a-c^2D already forces X=0. Put Z=Xc. The first
commutator gives Xb=DZ,Xa=D^2Z; the second gives
partial_a Z=-2bc Z, impossible for a nonzero polynomial by a-degree.
This is an all-degree zero-centralizer proof at the specified slice,
not an all-slice claim. Adapted nonlinear coordinates repair it.

The criterion can also succeed where656 fails: the original slice of
658's nonlinear-F/nonconstant-q family has common centralizer partial_c,
although658 excludes its complementary-basis certificate for every
slice/constant frame. These controls were polynomial from the start;
no unknown cancellation kernel has been recognized in this pass.

### Universal family and two failed lifting constructions

Source: research/origin-dilation-rees-and-polynomial-lifting-gap-pass701-working.md.
For any actual sliced input E=sum Pi(z)partial_zi on B=C^[4], with
Es=1 and s(0)=0, set E_t=sum Pi(tz)partial_zi and sigma=s(tz)/t.
The exact iterate identity

    E_t^j(zi)=t^(j-1)(E^j zi)(tz), j>=1,

proves local nilpotence, and E_t(sigma)=1. Its kernel is isomorphic
over C[t] to R=C[t,z]/(sigma). The relative gradient is unimodular,
so R is smooth, R/(t)=C^[3], R[t^-1]=A[t,t^-1], and R[v]=C[t]^[4].
Moreover R=A[t,m/t] for the maximal ideal of the selected point in
A=B/(s). Thus this is the standard extended Rees deformation to
the tangent space, with mixed weights wt(t)=1, wt(z_i)=-1 and R_0=A.

The precise remaining equivalence is

    A=C^[3] iff R=C[t]^[3]
             iff some delta in LND_C(R) satisfies delta(t)=1.

Requiring delta homogeneous of weight degree -1 gives the same
condition. A polynomial trivialization on a parameter neighborhood
or at the generic point would also recognize A by specialization.
The actual formal completion C[z1,z2,z3][[t]] does not supply any
of these algebraic trivializations.

The reused654 coordinate seed E=partial_x-2x partial_y,
s=x+(y+x^2)^2 gives an exact check inside the actual cylinder class.
Put U=y+t x^2 and V=sigma=x+tU^2; these have a whole polynomial
inverse. Nevertheless the canonical projected coordinate is
Y=rho_t(y)=U-t^3U^4. Its formal inverse has every coefficient
c_n positive in sum c_n t^(3n)Y^(3n+1), hence unbounded Y-degree
and no termination. This happens at fixed original coefficient
degree1, slice degree4 and generator nilpotence bound3.

The unconditional homogeneous horizontal derivation
D=partial_t-(partial_t sigma)E_t preserves the quotient relation.
On this example's R=C[t,U,z,w], it becomes
partial_t+t^2U^4 partial_U. Its nth iterate on U has nonzero highest
term product_(j=0)^(n-1)(3j+1) t^(2n)U^(3n+1), so it is not LND.
Both failures concern specified constructions; U itself provides
successful polynomial coordinates here. They neither disprove
cancellation nor obstruct all possible polynomial lifts.

### The standard-grading shortcut is exactly an already-constant action

CDDG Theorem5.13 requires a retract to be a graded subalgebra for
the STANDARD grading of a polynomial algebra, with an augmentation-
preserving retraction. Root read its entire statement and proof in
turn6546view0, not just its abstract. The mixed grading above is
different. [Primary theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.11023).

There is a sharper direct boundary for this particular family:

    K=ker E_t is standard-z-graded over C[t]
    if and only if E has constant coefficients in the supplied frame.

Proof. Let p=Pi(0) as a vector and ell=ds_0, so ell(p)=1.
The linear-z part of rho_t(zi) is L_i=zi-p_i ell. Terms with
Taylor index at least2 have z-order at least2; the index1 term has
linear part -p_i ell. If K is standard-graded, each L_i lies in K.
Thus Pi(tz)=p_i E_t(ell) for every i. At t=1, E=h E0, where
E0=sum p_i partial_zi and h=E(ell). The identity Es=1 gives
h(E0s)=1. Hence h is a nonzero constant, and evaluation at0 gives
h=ell(p)=1. Therefore E=E0. Conversely, a constant translation
has a kernel generated over C[t] by three linear forms.

The augmentation premise is automatic: rho_t((z)) is contained
in (z), because sigma has no constant z-term. It is the graded-
subalgebra premise that fails for every nonconstant action in this
frame. Choosing a successful nonlinear frame is still an unproved
global step. This lemma restricts a proposed application; it is not
a new recognition class. Geometry and General independently reconstructed
the entire argument after completing their701 reviews. General also
reread CDDG's complete theorem proof and Remark5.14 in turn6552view1:
the theorem requires a graded SUBALGEBRA, not a graded retraction.

That is an already recognized subclass, not a general consequence

### A genuine four-coordinate counterexample to the stronger shortcut

Source: research/full-orbit-coefficient-linear-extraction-obstruction-pass700-working.md.
On B=C[a,b,c,s] with E=partial_s, put

    t1=s+a^2, t2=t1+b^2, t3=t2+c^2,
    z=(a+t1^2,b+t2^2,c+t3^2,t3).

Six reverse shears give the whole polynomial inverse. All three
quadratic-flow coordinates have E^2(zi)=2 and E^3(zi)=0. For the
specified slice s, the ENTIRE invariant coefficient span is

    V=span_C{1,a^2,b^2,c^2,
             a+a^4,b+(a^2+b^2)^2,c+(a^2+b^2+c^2)^2}.

Every nonconstant member of V has an affine critical point. The
proof first removes variables whose linear-bearing coefficients
vanish. With three active variables, the homogenized gradients are
three cubics with only explicitly classified possible infinity
points. Their local intersection lengths total at most15, whereas
an entirely finite projective intersection has length27. The
two-variable case similarly gives at most3 at infinity versus total9.
The mixed-point resonance lengths5/6 and the axis length6/9 are
computed, not ignored. This excludes every coefficient vector,
including nongeneric choices, and every nonconstant affine-linear
extraction of an ambient coordinate or affine-plane fibration.

The count uses the standard complete-intersection Hilbert series.
Root read the displayed Stacks regular-sequence and polynomial-CM
licenses in turn6508view0/1 and Vakil Section2.2 in turn6506view0.
Krull's height theorem also excludes an empty projective intersection:
m positive-degree generators cannot have the irrelevant radical of
height m+1. The note's finite-intersection count retains this boundary.

### Exact criterion and its explicit limit

Source: research/projected-coordinate-completion-criterion-pass699-working.md.
For B=A[s]=C^[4], A=ker E, Es=1, the canonical retraction rho,
an ACTUAL frame F=(X1,X2,X3,U), and D=partial_U, put
H=(rho X1,rho X2,rho X3,s). Then

    det JH=(det JF)rho(Ds).

Moreover H is an automorphism iff rho(Ds) is a nonzero constant,
iff Ds is a nonzero constant. The determinant proof uses invariant
volume and reduction modulo s. The degree-in-U argument already
used in654 then gives s=cU+h(X1,X2,X3). An explicit whole inverse
uses F^{-1} on the zero section followed by the polynomial E-flow.
There is no appeal to the Jacobian conjecture, and the proof retains
the actual cylinder hypothesis. The functions criterion is distinct
from the projected-derivation criteria654/656.

For every k>=2 the fixed translation E=partial_u,s=u admits the
actual frame F_k=(a+b^k(u+a^k),b,c,u+a^k), with a full polynomial
inverse. It fixes the entire u-axis and satisfies the order-k
conditions of698, but exact projection gives Jacobian
1+k b^k a^(k-1), a nonunit. Thus arbitrary finite-order witnesses
cannot be completed automatically in this way. The standard frame
still solves this same action with degree one. This is NOT a lower
bound on minimum witness complexity or a cancellation counterexample.

Existence of some frame passing the criterion is equivalent to
coordinatehood of the supplied slice, hence to the original question
under the supplied cylinder identity. No general construction is
provided. The stronger idea of extracting a coordinate from the span
of all invariant orbit-Taylor coefficients remains unproved; the
earlier95 projected-generator example does not refute that stronger
idea, because its higher coefficients recover a coordinate.

### Recognition for the commuting constant-plus-quadratic subclass

This is a corollary of known kernel structure and invariant-coordinate
results, not a proposed new cancellation theorem. Let B=C^[4] with
its displayed standard grading, and suppose E=L+H is an LND with a
polynomial slice, L constant-coefficient, H homogeneous with quadratic
coefficients, and [L,H]=0. Then ker E is a polynomial three-ring.

The slice forces L!=0, since otherwise E vanishes at the origin.
A linear change makes L=partial_t and B=C[x,y,z,t]. Commutation
makes all coefficients of H independent of t. Its restriction D to
R=C[x,y,z] is therefore an ordinary homogeneous quadratic-coefficient
LND: it equals the restriction of E, so local nilpotence is inherited.
If D=0, x is already an E-invariant ambient linear coordinate.

If D!=0, the standard homogeneous-kernel and Jacobian descriptions give

    ker D=C[F,G],
    D=a*Jac(F,G,-),

with algebraically independent positive-degree homogeneous F,G and
a nonzero polynomial a. A nonzero Jacobian coefficient is homogeneous,
so comparison with D's homogeneous coefficients also makes a homogeneous.
The degree equation is

    2=deg(a)+deg(F)+deg(G)-2,

and hence deg(F)+deg(G)<=4. If either degree is one, the required
invariant linear form is immediate. Otherwise both are two. In the
pencil lambda F+mu G the determinant of the ternary quadratic matrix
is a homogeneous binary cubic, so some nonzero pair(lambda,mu) gives
a singular member over C (also when that determinant is identically
zero). Algebraic independence ensures that member is nonzero. A
singular ternary quadratic over C is a product of linear forms,
possibly repeated. Factorial closure of ker D forces each factor
to be D-invariant. This again supplies a nonzero invariant linear
form ell. No triangularization of a general four-variable action was
assumed, and reducible D is included through the factor a.

In either case E ell=0, and ell is an ACTUAL ambient coordinate of B.
The slice makes A=ker E regular: B=A[u] is regular and regularity
descends, equivalently the slice hypersurface is smooth because Eu=1.
Bhatwadekar--Gupta--Lokhande Theorem3.5 gives A=C[ell]^[2].

### Exact degree criterion, with the existential quantifier retained

In fixed original coordinates let e=max degree of E's coefficients.
If an actual frame of forward degree d satisfies the order-k conditions
and k>e+d-1, all residuals are zero. Their total degrees are at most
e+d-1, whereas membership in I^k implies vanishing to order k at any
point of the orbit. Translation of that point to the origin proves the
contradiction for every nonzero residual. No inverse-degree compactness
argument or constant-Jacobian-to-invertibility inference is used.

Let mu(k) be the least forward degree over ALL such frames. It is
finite by extension and nondecreasing. If an exact frame exists with
least degree d_*, then mu(k)=d_* for k>e+d_*-1. Otherwise
mu(k)>=k-e+1 for every k. No bound forcing the first alternative is
proved. This is an exact conditional criterion, not recognition of a
previously unresolved cylinder.

Even algebraic formal data need not have bounded-degree realizations.
For standard E=partial_u, the rational formal map
(x/(1+x),(1+x)^2 y,z,u) has inverse
(X/(1-X),(1-X)^2Y,Z,U), determinant one and compatible extendable
finite jets. No polynomial realizes all of them, and every order-k
lift has degree>=k-1. These are PRESCRIBED jets; mu(k)=1 for this
already-standard E. The difference between a chosen family and the
minimum over all frames is essential.

The degree argument also works for a single transverse ambient
coordinate X: EX in I^k and k>e+deg X-1 imply EX=0. Then the
already-retained Bhatwadekar--Gupta--Lokhande Theorem3.5 recognizes
the regular sliced kernel. Root freshly read its exact statement and
complete displayed proof in turn6376view0; no existence of such X
follows. The theorem requires an ACTUAL ambient coordinate, not a
regular local parameter. [Primary BGL source](https://arxiv.org/html/1501.01438v1).

### A smooth invariant does not license relative finite-jet extension

This is a full all-order countercontrol INSIDE ordinary polynomial
space, not an exotic cylinder. Put

    B=C[x,y,z,u], E=partial_u,
    f=x+x^2 y-1, I=(x-1,y,z).

The function f is invariant, vanishes at the base point(1,0,0),
and is smooth everywhere: its two nonzero gradient entries
(1+2xy,x^2) never vanish simultaneously. For c!=-1 its fiber
is C* times A2, since x is invertible and y=(c+1-x)/x^2.
Smoothness does not give the needed fiberwise additive transitivity.

In fact EVERY polynomial automorphism phi fixing f fixes x and y,
with arbitrary mixing of z,u permitted. Unique factorization of
f+1=x(1+xy) makes phi permute these prime factors up to constants.
They cannot be interchanged: B/(x)=C[y,z,u] has only constant units,
whereas B/(1+xy)=C[x,x^-1,z,u] has nonconstant units. Thus
phi(x)=cx and phi(1+xy)=c^-1(1+xy). Reducing
1+cx phi(y)=c^-1(1+xy) modulo x gives c=1, then phi(y)=y.

Nevertheless for EVERY integer N>=2, put t=z^N and w=1-tx.
There is the formal I-adic automorphism

    H_N=(x/w, y*w^2-t*w, z, u).

Its inverse is the same formula with t replaced by -t, since z
is unchanged. The identity 1+H_N(x)H_N(y)=w(1+xy) proves
H_N(f)=f. The x,y Jacobian block has determinant w^-2*w^2=1;
the other diagonal block is identity, so t's dependence on z does
not alter the full determinant. It commutes with E. The denominator
w is an I-adic unit, and all changes lie in I^N. But

    H_N(x)-x=t*x^2/w = z^N modulo I^(N+1),

which is nonzero. No f-preserving polynomial automorphism can
realize this order-(N+1) jet, since every such automorphism fixes x
exactly. Unrestricted KU extension DOES apply to the volume jet on
the standard orbit line. This proves that a relative-preservation
version cannot simply be inserted into the general argument.

Source: research/two-stage-y-fiber-rigidity-and-euler-profile-pass685-working.md.

These surfaces are the blowups of the plane at q transverse smooth points
of the cusp v^n+w^q=0, minus its strict transform. The cusp complement
has the finite-etale Kummer cover G_m times {V^n+W^q=1}, whose second
factor is a genus(n-1)(q-1)/2 curve minus one point. Its log Kodaira
dimension is1. At the q blowup centers the exceptional curves are KEPT
in the open surface, so K_new+D_new=pi^*(K_old+D_old). Consequently
log_kappa(S_(n,q))=1 as well.

A Ga-action on S_(n,q) times ANY affine ell-space moving a surface
function would cover a dense open subset of S by nonconstant affine-line
images, contradicting this logarithmic Kodaira dimension. The argument
does not assume preservation of the surface subring. Fiberwise application
and dense specialization prove every y-fixed LND on R[u1,...,u_ell]
annihilates R. On the open y!=1, unit fixation makes this the entire class.
Thus its exact ML is R[(y-1)^(-1)]. For ell=1 every action is exactly
h*partial_u over that base. This excludes the WHOLE chart action route,
not just the narrower y,z-fixed genus-one route initially considered.

### Actual-polynomial control: compatible translations need not give an affine torus

Let B0=C[x,y,z,t] and

    E=partial_t+t^2*partial_x+(t^4+t)*partial_y+t^6*partial_z.

The slice is t and the exact kernel is

    K=C[x-t^3/3, y-t^5/5-t^2/2, z-t^7/7].

These generators with t have a triangular polynomial inverse, proving
K=C^[3] without cancellation. The ambient translations partial_x,
partial_y,partial_z already preserve K and induce a complete commuting
intrinsic translation frame. Nevertheless no positive-dimensional
affine-linear torus preserves this embedded K, in ANY affine frame.

Here is the full infinitesimal argument. Write X=(x,y,z) and
f(t)=(t^2,t^4+t,t^6). A general affine derivation M has

    M(t)=rho*X+alpha*t+beta, M(X)=N*X+v*t+c.

If M(K) is contained in K, then [M,E]=hE because B0=K[t]. Its t
component forces h=-rho*f-alpha. Comparing X-dependent terms in the
other components gives f_i'(t)*rho*X=0 and hence rho=0. Thus

    N*f+v=(alpha*t+beta)*f'+alpha*f.

The first row forces N13=N12=0, beta=0, N11=3alpha and v1=0.
The second row's t^4 and t coefficients would require N22=5alpha
and N22=2alpha, so alpha=0. The independent functions 1,t^2,t^4+t,t^6
then force N=v=0. Only the three translations c remain. A nonzero torus
Lie generator is semisimple, whereas a nonzero translation is locally
nilpotent; hence no positive-dimensional affine-linear torus acts this
way. The same coefficient independence gives K intersect Span(1,x,y,z,t)=C.

For any SUPPLIED torus T on an actual B=A[s] with B*=C*, the exact
compatibility condition is T(A)=A iff E=partial_s is a T-weight vector.
Indeed preservation of A forces g(s)=c*s+h(A), c in C*, by degree
comparison with g^(-1); hence gEg^(-1) is a constant multiple of E.
Conversely this conjugation property preserves the kernel.

The control has a nonlinear compatible torus, obtained by using its
displayed triangular coordinates. It refutes an AFFINE selection shortcut,
not intrinsic torus existence or nonlinear conjugation in general.
General derived the hand proof and exact checkbd694a:20 affine coefficients
plus an independent constant commutator factor, rank18/21. Root d1b36a
substituted that factor first and got rank17/20. Both kernels consist
exactly of the same three translation directions; the counts agree.

### Accepted682: exact Euler profile for EVERY polynomial in H

Source: research/two-stage-all-plane-functions-euler-profile-pass682-working.md.
For B=C[a,b,x,K,S]/(a²S+a(1+x+x²K)+x⁴+b³), H=C[x,b], and ANY f in H,
put g(t)=f(t³,-t⁴). For every complex lambda, the complete formula is

    chi_c(V_B(f-lambda))=chi_c({t in C:g(t)=lambda}).

The open a!=0 piece is V_H(f-lambda) times C* times A1, so contributes0.
The a=0 piece is V_H(x⁴+b³,f-lambda) times A2. The cusp parametrization
t->(t³,-t⁴) is bijective, with inverse -b/x away from its origin. For
nonconstant g the answer is exactly the number of DISTINCT roots; for
constant g=gamma it is1 at gamma and0 elsewhere. Scheme multiplicities
do not enter the compact-support Euler characteristic.

Every nonconstant g in C[t³,t⁴] has degree at least3, so the generic
value is either0 or at least3. A global coordinate would have every fiber
of Euler characteristic1, which excludes EVERY nonconstant f in H.
The same stratification gives chi_c(B)=1. A slice of any global LND would
make B=(ker delta)[f] and every fiber have Euler characteristic1, so it
is excluded as well. This does not say LNDs kill H or preserve H.

This proof is shorter and stronger than the preliminary curve-retract /
divisor-class approach. It needs no assumption that f is a coordinate
of H, no finite-degree bound, no Abhyankar--Moh theorem, and no claim
that a fiber of Euler characteristic1 must be affine space. For f=x+b
the generic value is4, with exact exceptions2 at0 and3 at27/256.

### Accepted682: the same no-slice property occurs in a smooth retract of C4

In B'=C[X,Y,Z,T] put p=X+X²Y, q=Z+Z²T. The retract H'=C[p,q] has
retraction (X,Y,Z,T)->(p,0,q,0). The quotient map (p,q):A4->A2 is
smooth everywhere, because its two nonvanishing Jacobian rows have
disjoint variable supports, and it has the section (p,q)->(p,0,q,0).

For EVERY polynomial F(p,q), the exact Euler profile of F=lambda is
1 when lambda=F(0,0), and0 otherwise. Stratifying by X and Z zero or
nonzero gives three strata with a C* factor and one A2 stratum at
lambda=F(0,0). Thus no nonconstant element of H' is an ambient
coordinate or a slice of any LND, even though B' is literally polynomial.
This rules out the proposed general recognition shortcut, not the actual
sliced-kernel hypotheses: H' is not factorially closed, has dimension2,
and the retraction kernel is (Y,T), not principal.

The individual generator X+X²Y is explicitly published by Shpilrain--Yu
on printed p.477 of [Polynomial Retracts and the Jacobian Conjecture](https://shpilrain.ccny.cuny.edu/retracts.pdf).
Our control is a product of that known example; its all-function Euler
profile is separately proved, not attributed to their paper. Root read

### Accepted681: all generic-line repairs retaining x,b, and individual noncoordinates

The exact whole presentation is

    B=C[a,b,x,K,S]/(a²S+a(1+x+x²K)+x⁴+b³).

Over C(x,b,K) its generic fiber is the Laurent line; thus no nonzero
C[x,b,K]-linear LND exists and that embedded triple cannot be completed.
The continuation strengthens this: over F=C(x,b), the ring is
F[a,a^(-1),K], so even retaining only the pair x,b cannot give coordinates.

More precisely, put H=C[x,b], P=x⁴+b³, A=1+x+x²K+aS. The LND
delta=a partial_K-x² partial_S has exact kernel U=H[a,A]/(aA+P).
Reduction modulo a proves U intersect aB=aU, and descending denominators
gives the full kernel and B intersect F(a)=U. Its H-basis is
1,a^i,A^j for positive i,j. For EVERY f algebraically independent from
x,b, the generic fiber over H[f] is A1 if and only if

    f=alpha(x,b)*a+beta(x,b), or f=gamma(x,b)*A+beta(x,b),

with the corresponding alpha or gamma nonzero. A generic A1 fiber forces
its unit a into F(f); algebraic closure in F(a,K) then forces F(f)=F(a).
The Laurent basis and degree-one rational-map condition prove the entire
classification. Every listed projection omits f=beta over base points
where P*alpha or P*gamma is nonzero. This is not a bounded-degree search.

The strongest single-function test is direct. For every nonzero lambda,
the fiber x=lambda is the smooth domain
C[a,b,W,S]/(aW+b³+lambda⁴), with three reduced a-divisor components.
Its a-localization is a UFD with units c*a^n, so the full divisor class
group is Z³/Z(1,1,1)=Z². For every nonzero mu, b=mu has four reduced
a-divisor components and the same unit argument gives Z³. Thus neither
x nor b individually can be a coordinate. Changing both functions is not
excluded, and a bad projection does not prove ambient nonpolynomiality.

### A known torus criterion, with its missing compatibility made explicit

[Berchtold--Hausen Theorem3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0209405)
diagonalizes an effective rank-three torus on an actual affine four-space.
For B=A[u]=C^[4], let S scale u and fix A. An effective rank-three torus
T containing S preserves B0=A and B1=Au. Constant units give
t(u)=chi(t)u with chi restricted to S the identity. Thus T=ker(chi) times S,
and ker(chi) is a connected faithful rank-two torus on A. Conversely such
an intrinsic torus products with S. Diagonalizing T makes Fix(S)=Spec(A)
a three-dimensional linear subspace. This proves the conditional
recognition result without any maximality assumption. Polynomiality of
B supplies some rank-four torus, not containment of this particular S.
The older644 already retains the slice-torus linearization equivalence.

[Gaifullin--Petrov Lemma6.1 and Section11](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.13593)
give the same known complexity-one exclusion via maximal tori. A genuinely
maximal rank-three torus anywhere on a candidate cylinder would also
exclude affine four-space, but maximality within a chosen subgroup is
insufficient. No such torus is supplied here. Root read the complete
relevant BH proof inturn6146view0 and GP lemma/deduction inturn6148view0;

linearization proof has not been reconstructed. This is a source audit,

### Additional bounded action evidence, not an all-action theorem

Jet gave two exact exclusions on the coarse-graded Cox ring from678.
Root reconstructed their proofs, including the exact kernel contractions.
These statements do not classify arbitrary coarse-degree-zero LNDs.
Write E=q³*partial_p+3p²vT*partial_w and
F=p³v*partial_q+3q²w*partial_T.

First, for any finite composition phi of flows killing p, reduction modulo
p makes q a unit, so phi(q)=q modulo p. Consequently phi E phi^(-1)
sends p to q³ modulo p. Every coarse homogeneous component except weight
-4 sends p into (p). If such a component is locally nilpotent it must kill
p. This covers arbitrary p-fixed flow sequences of the BARE E, not replicas
of E or arbitrary sums or content divisions.

Second, take nonzero homogeneous g in ker E=C[q,v,T] and h in
ker F=C[p,v,w]; zero replicas are trivial.
Every coarse-zero coefficient C_j of exp(t hF)(gE)exp(-t hF) that is an
LND kills p. For j>=1 its values on p,h,w are respectively h^j/j! times
F^j(gq³), F^j(gE(h)), and 3p²vF^j(gT). If h is not in C[v], the
coefficient of t³ in exp(tF)E(h) is p⁸v³(p h_p+3w h_w), nonzero, so its
F-degree is3. Thus C_j(h)=0 iff C_j(p)=0; divisibility by h and local
nilpotence force both. In the remaining homogeneous case h=c*v^d,
weight(g)=-r gives weight(C_j)=-r-4+j(1-3d). Only d=0,j=r+4 can give
zero weight. Modulo w the F-flow fixes T and translates q, while
deg_q(g)<=r<j. Hence w divides C_j(w), forcing it zero under local
nilpotence. Equal F-degrees of Tg and q³g then force C_j(p)=0.
This covers ONE conjugation of homogeneous replicas, not arbitrary
iterations, recombinations or division by content. Jet's fresh whole
checks1c9bf4 support those identities; no frozen checker was used.

### Polynomial-cylinder premise: a necessary test passes in the displayed coordinates

Root personally recovered the complete stated Main Theorem of Mulay,
[*Monolinear hyperplanes*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jalgebra.2026.05.043),
in primary publisher result turn6085search0. Its Section5 proof was not
accessible and has NOT been fully audited. The actual presentation676 is
monolinear with X=a, Y=S, d=2, Z=(V,b,k), and residual g=V⁴+b³.
Thus it fits the theorem's form under a hypothetical B=C^[4].

The stated necessary tests all pass in these coordinates. The polynomial
g is irreducible. Its generic curve b³+V⁴-t is geometrically integral:
over an algebraic closure of C(t), t-V⁴ has simple zeros, so is not a cube
in the rational V-field. The cubic binomial is irreducible. Consequently
C(V,b,k)/C(g) is regular in characteristic zero. Every weighted leading
form H is V⁴, b³, or V⁴+b³. Every factor q considered in the theorem is
independent of k, since degree in k is zero. Taking L=C(V,b) shows
C(V,b,k)=L(k) is ruled, hence separably uniruled, over C(H) and C(q).
This is a verified failure of these necessary tests to obstruct the displayed
presentation. It is not a proof of polynomiality, a sufficiency claim, or an
audit of every possible coordinate change or alternate presentation.

The related [Dubouloz--Heden--Kishimoto extension theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1707.08768)
requires a proper selected Ga-action in its Definition3.1/TypeII and Theorem3.7.
For the natural projection X->A2_(V,b), the selected whole action
b³ partial_T - V² partial_S fixes P pointwise. Its stabilizers there are Ga,
so it is not proper. The theorem does not extend arbitrary complement actions
across this P. Root read the exact definition and theorem inturn6093view0/1;
Geometry also read the whole theorem proof. This is a hypothesis-scope check.

### Accepted668: exact models and an actual finite proof obligation

Source: research/squarefree-plinth-divisor-envelope-pass668-working.md.
Let A be a finite-type complex UFD of dimension three, D a primitive
nonzero LND, C=ker D=C[a,b], and full plinth pC with p=product f_i
nonconstant squarefree. Fix the actual minimal slice r with Dr=p.
No polynomial-cylinder hypothesis is needed for the following proof.

At O_i=C_(f_i), the residue ring of A is a one-dimensional domain
with nonzero LND. Its invariant field is finite separable over
kappa_i=Frac(C/f_i). Lift the monic minimal polynomial G_i of rbar
and put y_i=G_i(r)/f_i. The ring H=O_i[r,y_i] has exact relation
f_i y_i=G_i(r). Its reduction injects into the actual residue ring,
because Dbar(y_i) is nonzero. Thus H intersect f_i A_i=f_i H.
Both rings become K[r] on inverting f_i, so minimal-denominator
descent proves A_i=H, not merely a dense inclusion. The residue
field is generated by the supplied rbar and has degree d_i>=2.

The distinct-degree monic basis gives, for EVERY n,

    I_n**=h_n C,   h_n=product_i f_i^(n-floor(n/d_i)),
    I_n=h_n J_n,  (J_n)_(q)=C_(q) at every height-one base prime.

Finite generation of A spreads each entire embedded monic model
to one principal open D(c_i), c_i notin(f_i), with the other f_j
inverted. These fixed opens and D(p) contain every height-one
point. Therefore ONE finite closed set Z supports ALL C/J_n.
This strengthens the initial per-degree support statement.

Set N=lcm(d_i). Then h_(n+N)=h_n h_N, and the exact Leibniz
formula gives I_n I_N subset I_(n+N). Consequently

    all I_n principal  iff  J_0=...=J_N=C.

If actual witnesses e_j satisfy D^j e_j=j!h_j for 0<=j<=N,
then e_(qN+j)=e_N^q e_j, 0<=j<N, supplies a C-basis in every
degree. It also makes A free of rank N over C[e_N]. This is
not an assertion that this finite extension is a polynomial ring.
No finite numerical experiment is substituted for these proofs.

The normal-UFD height-one intersection also proves all F_n finite
reflexive and hence free over the polynomial plane. It does NOT
make their quotient image ideals reflexive. The module-freeness
conclusion was already retained in102 under actual flatness; the
normal-UFD proof here drops that premise. The local curve statement

### Accepted667: all automorphisms preserving the invariant three-ring

Source: research/nonfence-invariant-ring-stabilizer-normal-form-pass667-working.md.
Let B=A[u], E=partial_u, with A a finite-type complex UFD, D primitive
nonzero LND, C=ker_A D=C[a,b], and full plinth pC. Assume p is not a
polynomial in any plane coordinate and B*=C*. Put S=C[u]. No assumption
LND(A)=CD is needed. Then EVERY automorphism phi with phi(S)=S has a
unique factorization

    phi=exp(P(u)D) o psi,
    P in uC[u],   psi|A=alpha,
    psi(u)=lambda u+h,
    alpha D alpha^(-1)=cD,
    lambda,c nonzero constants, h in C.

Conversely all such data give an S-preserving automorphism. This is
setwise equality of S, not mere inclusion. No bound on degrees or a
tameness hypothesis is used. The proof does not classify maps moving S.

Here is the mechanism. Same-kernel primitive saturation makes
phi D phi^(-1)=cD. Preservation of the full plinth gives phi(p)=mu p.
Inside S, the ring C is EXACTLY the intersection of kernels of all LNDs
killing p:665's general plane lemma supplies one inclusion and partial_u
the other. That characterization forces phi(C)=C, not merely phi(S)=S.
One-variable automorphism theory then gives phi(u)=lambda u+h(C).

By665, E'=phi E phi^(-1)=q(u)D+lambda^(-1)E. Choose the unique P(0)=0
with P_u=-lambda q. For tau=exp(PD), the exact conjugation identity is
tau E tau^(-1)=E-P_u D, hence tau^(-1)phi scales E and preserves A.
This produces alpha and the factorization. A constant term in P could
be absorbed into alpha, which explains the normalization and uniqueness.

The full conjugacy orbit of E under this stabilizer is exactly
{beta E+q(u)D: beta a nonzero CONSTANT, q in C[u]}. Its kernels are
exp(PD)(A). Subtracting beta E and extracting coefficients or specializing
u gives only C-multiples of D. This closes that entire
conjugation-and-coefficient construction for producing a second intrinsic
direction, not arbitrary frame repair or arbitrary ambient automorphisms.

There is deliberately no naive semidirect-product assertion: translating
u creates a constant term in P(u+h), which must be absorbed into alpha.
The full replica subgroup exp(C[u]D) intersects the lifted intrinsic
normalizer in exp(CD).

The hypothesis boundary has an exact whole-coordinate control. For
D=x*partial_y+y*partial_z on C[x,y,z,u], S=C[x,2xz-y^2,u] and the
plinth xC is a fence. The map z -> z+u preserves S and D, but moves
the plane by 2xz-y^2 -> 2xz-y^2+2xu. Thus the non-fence condition
cannot simply be deleted. The base in this control is polynomial;
it is not a cancellation counterexample.

### Accepted666: an affine-linear intrinsic action suffices

Source: research/affine-linear-intrinsic-action-recognition-pass666-working.md.
If a nonzero intrinsic LND L, extended by L(u)=0, is affine-linear in
some ACTUAL polynomial coordinates of B=A[u]=C^[4], then A=C^[3].
This is conditional recognition, not existence of that action or frame.

Write L(X)=NX+b; N is nilpotent. Without a fixed point, a linear
functional supplies an actual linear L-slice q. Hence ker_B L=B/(q)=C^[3].
E=partial_u restricts nontrivially there since u is L-invariant and
E(u)=1. Its kernel is C^[2] by the three-variable kernel theorem.
Evaluating q at u=0 supplies an intrinsic slice, finishing recognition.

With a fixed point z, commutation gives N E(z)=0, du_z N=0, and
du_z(E(z))=1. Thus ker N is not contained in im N, forcing a size-one
Jordan block. The only nonzero types are (2,1,1) and (3,1). The first
has image ideal (x). For the second, L=x*partial_y+y*partial_z and
h=2xz-y^2 give ker L=C[x,h,w] and ker L^2=ker L plus y*ker L.
Clearing minimal x-denominators and separating even/odd y terms proves
both; the FULL plinth is x*ker L. E preserves the relevant ideal, so
LND divisibility forces E(x)=0. The regular-kernel theorem gives
A=C[x]^[2]. No localized coordinate is substituted for a global one.

Primary inputs: Bhatwadekar--Gupta--Lokhande, arXiv:1501.01438v1,
Theorems2.3 and3.5, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.01438v1 .
Root read the exact2.3 statement in21e753 and all Section3 through3.5,
its proof and limitations inf03429. Theorem2.3 is quoted there from
Miyanishi; its original proof was not newly reconstructed. Both reviewers
independently checked the cited scope.

The corollary assumes a finite-dimensional abelian LND space H normalized
by this nonzero intrinsic L. Generic rank four gives a closed open orbit,
hence transitivity. Effective abelian transitivity yields actual
translation coordinates; normalization makes L affine-linear. E need NOT
belong to H. Rank three and existence of H are not supplied.

### Accepted664: the degree-one apparent escape is impossible

Source: research/degree-one-commuting-orbit-tangent-exclusion-pass664-working.md.
Let A be a three-dimensional characteristic-zero domain, p a smooth
rational L-fixed point, and T an ambient LND whose L-conjugates commute.
Put C_j=(ad L)^j T/j!, M=dL_p, v=T(p,0)_horizontal. Then
deg_L T(u)=1 implies M^2v=0.

The main step does not need the degree premise. If M^2v!=0, flowing the
WHOLE fixed cylinder line (p,s) under C0,C1,C2 gives a map with rank-four
differential, hence a dominant map. For j>=3, C_j vanishes on that line
by M^3=0 and commutes with these flows. Dominance makes C_j vanish
globally, so actual adjoint order is two. The pullback F of u is invariant
under (t0,t1,t2,s) -> (t0,t1+r*t0,t2+2*r*t1+r^2*t0,s).
For vertical degree one, C2(u)=0 makes F independent of t2, and this
identity then forces independence of t1. Dominance would force C1(u)=0,
contradicting degree one.

The exact surviving success cases in the certified constant span are
T(u)=0 with v!=0, or nonzero L-invariant T(u) with Mv!=0. Every
non-invariant vertical speed fails to recover a tangent at p. This is
not a classification of other repairs or all intrinsic actions.

### Accepted665: exact centralizer and abelian-family restriction

Source: research/rank-one-abelian-vertical-kernel-rigidity-pass665-working.md.
Explicit hypotheses: A a finite-type complex UFD; D primitive nonzero
LND; C=ker D=C[a,b]; full plinth(D)=pC with p nonconstant and not a
polynomial in any plane coordinate. Without a rank-one premise,

    {W LND(A[u]): [D,W]=0}=C[u]D+C E,  E=partial_u.

Coefficients of E are arbitrary elements of C, not just units.
Every module member is LND; members need not commute. The full plinth
extends to pC[u]; commutation and LND divisibility give Wp=0. The
non-fence plane lemma forces WC=0. Primitive saturation and the
one-variable LND degree test finish the equality and its converse.

The plane lemma works even for an LND on ANY finite-type complex domain
containing C, without preserving C. A projected nonconstant additive orbit
over a smooth value of p lies in a smooth plane-fiber component. Projective
completion makes that component A1; Abhyankar--Moh--Suzuki makes its
equation a coordinate g. Factorial closure gives Wg=0. Writing p in
C[g,h], the equation 0=Wp=p_h Wh would force p in C[g], a contradiction.
This reuses651's plane mechanism, not a new surface classification.
Root read its exact passage in3cc557 and reopened Palka Theorem B at
https://arxiv.org/html/1405.5391v2 (turn5828view0). Root reread all35
in7acf7c. Both reviewers independently checked the plane-theorem scope.

With the ADDITIONAL hypothesis LND(A)=CD, inherited35 classifies ambient
LNDs killing u as q(u)D. If an abelian H contains nonzero qD, then
[W,qD]=0 gives [W,D]=-(Wq/q)D. Primitive saturation makes Wq/q polynomial;
LND divisibility gives Wq=0. Thus all H centralizes D, lies in the displayed
module and has generic rank at most two. Otherwise its vertical map is
injective and no nonzero constant combination descends. No generic rank
bound in the injective branch is proved.

### Combined664/665 corollary: no rank-three orbit along the fixed line

Retain665's primitive/kernel/full-non-fence-plinth hypotheses. Its extra
assumption LND(A)=CD is NOT needed here. Let p be a smooth D-fixed
threefold point and let the D-conjugates of an ambient LND T commute.
Set C_j=(ad D)^j T/j!, M=dD_p, v=T(p,0)_horizontal.

Suppose M^2v!=0. The degree-independent dominance argument of664 makes
C_j=0 globally for j>=3. Then C2 is an LND centralizing D. By665,
C2=q(u)D+beta E with q in C[u] and beta in C. Since D(p)=0, its value
at (p,0) is vertical. But the exact tangent formula is
C2(p,0)=(M^2v/2,0), a nonzero horizontal vector. Contradiction.
Therefore M^2v=0. Apply the same proof after each constant slice shift:
M^2v(s)=0 all along (p,s). Every C_j for j>=2 vanishes there, so this
ENTIRE SINGLE conjugation span has tangent rank at most two along
the fixed line. This does not bound arbitrary combined families or
points outside Fix(D).

Root reconstructed this deduction; General and Jet independently checked
it and both confirmed the rank-one premise is unnecessary. It excludes
this specific proposed rank-three fixed-orbit route under the stated
hypotheses. It supplies none of those hypotheses universally.

### Accepted662: quotient compatibility is an exact coefficient tail

Source: research/commuting-orbit-coefficient-tangent-test-pass662-working.md.
For an intrinsic LND L extended by L(u)=0 and ambient LND T, write
C_j=(ad L)^j(T)/j! and T_t=sum t^j C_j. The finite identities
[T,(ad L)^j T]=0 are equivalent to pairwise commutation of all
conjugates, and to commutation of all C_j. Interpolation of commuting
LNDs then certifies every constant combination as an LND.

Let h=T(u), e=deg_L h if h is nonzero, and e=-1 otherwise. Root's
additional reconstruction found the decisive simplification:
h,Lh,...,L^e h are linearly independent over the constant field.
Successive application of powers of L proves this in all degrees.
Consequently the combination sum c_j C_j descends through (u)
EXACTLY when c_0=...=c_e=0. LND divisibility makes preservation of
(u) equivalent to killing u. Quotient descent need not be restriction
to the embedded A. No cancellation of lower vertical coefficients
by higher coefficients is possible within this single orbit.

At a smooth L-fixed point p, put M=dL_p and let v be the horizontal
part of T(p,0). The j-th coefficient has horizontal value
(-M)^j v/j!, and zero vertical value for j>=1. The tangent Ga
representation gives M^3=0 on a threefold. Hence the entire certified
span recovers a nonzero intrinsic tangent if and only if
M^(e+1)v is nonzero. The first surviving coefficient itself suffices.
For e>=2 recovery is impossible. The degree-one row is a conditional
test; no general attainability or impossibility claim is made.

The complete whole control L=a*partial_b+b*partial_c and
T=partial_a+c*partial_u has a commuting orbit with coefficients
T, -partial_b+b*partial_u, (partial_c+a*partial_u)/2. Their values
at the origin span three tangent directions, but their vertical
values c,b,a/2 are independent, so no nonzero combination descends.
A separate inverse-certified control shows that taking whole-family
differences before u-top extraction can recover a direction that
all the individual u-tops miss. Neither control has a point fixed
by EVERY intrinsic LND, so neither refutes that stronger premise.

The note also proves why naive top stripping is not nilpotence-safe:
if the highest vertical coefficient h_q is nonzero, subtracting only
u^q D_q violates the horizontal/vertical LND degree bound. Subtracting
the full u^q(D_q+h_q E) is not a sum of certified LNDs either.

### Accepted660: a proper reduced ideal can still give a false positive

Source: research/proper-higher-derivative-ideal-nonsection-control-pass660-working.md.
For every nonconstant q in k[b] and nonlinear F in k[x], the whole frame

    x=a+q*u, y=b, z=c+q*u^2, t=u+F(x)

because E^2z=2q and all other higher coordinate derivatives are
q-multiples. The necessary test659 passes: Et-1=qF'(x) lies in J.
Taking q=b makes J proper, nonzero, and reduced.

Nevertheless every possible polynomial graph and constant normal
would force lambda_t=1 and

    lambda_x + F'(a-qh) - 2*lambda_z*h = 0.

For quadratic F, a nonconstant polynomial in b would have to divide
a polynomial whose a-coefficient is a nonzero scalar. For higher F,
the a-degree of F'(a-qh) strictly exceeds that of h. The possible
degree-one cancellation would require q to be a unit, contrary to
the hypothesis. Thus NO h and NO linear frame succeeds, before any
commutation condition is imposed. The normalizer correspondence659
extends this to polynomial frame changes preserving the embedded A.

Only one elementary shear, z=c+q*u^2, distinguishes the frame from658.

eta nonzero: h=a/(b+eta). It is a b-adic series and regular on
D(b+eta), but not polynomial on the entire base. This only verifies
the normal equation, not a commuting projected basis.

### Accepted661: the exact first formal obstruction and whole controls

Source: research/residual-normal-formal-graph-lifting-gap-pass661-working.md.
Fix a constant direction ell passing659 and write G(T)=E(ell)(T)-1
in I[T]. Its derivative is also in I[T], so the raw implicit-function
unit-derivative test is unavailable modulo proper I. A formal graph
first needs a residue root of [G(T)] in (I/I^2)[T]. This is exactly
the section condition modulo I^2, not merely an informal warning.
The full square-zero correction equation is Q(s)+Q'(s)*epsilon=0.
For principal I=(f), divide G=fQ. The proof establishes that f stays
regular in the completion; a residue root of Q with unit derivative
has a unique f-adic lift by the written recursive construction.
There is no assertion that this lift is rational or polynomial.

The actual whole frame

    x=a+b*u, y=b, z=c+b*u^m, t=u+x^2, m>=3,

has the inverse u=t-x^2, a=x-yu, c=z-yu^m, b=y and full J=(y).
The residual test passes. But any constant direction with a formal
section u=s along b=0 would force lambda_t=1 and then

    lambda_x + m*lambda_z*s0^(m-1) + 2*a = 0.

If lambda_z=0 this is impossible; otherwise the valuation at
a+lambda_x/2 is one, excluding an (m-1)st power. Thus there is
NO section even in k(a,c)[[b]], for ANY constant direction. The
failure is at the first conormal stage, with a proper reduced ideal.
It is global along the divisor. It is not an assertion that all
closed-point formal sections fail: choosing suitable constants gives
the residue root1 with unit derivative at any k-rational point.

direction has the rational formal graph s=-a/(1+b). Changing only
the last coordinate to t=u+x^3 gives a direction with formal graph

    h=(1+3*a*b-sqrt(1+6*a*b))/(3*b^2), h=-s,

whose residue is 3*a^2/2. The square root is the branch congruent
to1 modulo b. The valuation of 1+6ab proves this selected root is
not rational. These are three distinct boundaries: residual to
formal, formal to rational, and rational to global polynomial.

but not that g is a coordinate. The explicit whole-coordinate

### A general limit on enlarging the ideal over nonlinear frames

There is no nontrivial obstruction obtained by summing these ideals
over every polynomial coordinate frame. Here is the complete reason,
valid over every characteristic-zero field in ambient dimension N>=2.
The coordinate polynomials span the entire polynomial ring as a
k-vector space. For positive degree d, the finite polarization identity

    d! * l1*...*ld
      = sum_{S subset {1,...,d}} (-1)^(d-|S|) (sum_{i in S} li)^d

expresses each monomial as a finite linear combination of powers L^d
of linear forms. For each nonzero L, choose an independent linear
form M and complete (L,M) to a linear frame. Both M and M+L^d are
coordinates, the latter by one elementary shear with its polynomial
inverse. Their difference is L^d. Constants are coordinate differences
as well. Thus u^2 is a FINITE constant-linear combination of such
coordinate polynomials f_i. Applying E twice yields

    2 = E^2(u^2) = sum_i c_i E^2(f_i).

Every term belongs to the higher-derivative ideal of a corresponding
actual frame. Their finite sum of ideals is therefore B. Linear
changes followed by one elementary shear already suffice for this
conclusion. It does not exhibit a SINGLE frame with J=0, J=B, a
unit normal, or a commuting complementary basis. It only shows
that the proposed all-frame sum cannot be a useful obstruction.

Root reconstructed this argument; Geometry independently checked
the complete finite polarization proof and exact ideal implication.
The dimension restriction matters: for N=1 every coordinate is
affine-linear, and E=partial_X has J=0 in every coordinate frame.
The unit-ideal argument needs only E(u)=1, not local nilpotence.
Bounded archive search69439a found no identical retained argument;
this elementary consequence is not claimed novel and needs no
additional numbered family note.

### A published obstruction to the simplest cuspidal-plinth lift

For p=x^d+z^a!=0, d,a>=2, any LND fixing a nonzero multiple of
p fixes x and z, even after finitely many polynomial variables
are added. Factorial closure first fixes p. Its polynomial orbit
coordinates F,G over the fraction field satisfy F^d+G^a=p.
They are coprime. Differentiation forces F^(d-1) to divide G'
and G^(a-1) to divide F'. Positive degrees r,s would give
(d-2)r+(a-2)s<=-2, impossible; if one is constant so is the other.

Geometry located the exact published Mini-Mason antecedent, not a
new theorem: [Finston-Maubach, Lemma2.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0706.4184).
Root read the full statement and proof and adjoining Lemmas1.1/2.2
in turn5700view0. This prevents a plinth-multiple-preserving auxiliary
action from moving the cuspidal base, not arbitrary cylinder actions.
No new numbered note or novelty claim was made for this application.

### Accepted647: an all-degree, prescribed-preservation obstruction

For B=C[x,y,z,t], f=x+x^m y+P, P=z^p+t^q and m,p,q>=2, there is
no regular retraction U -> X=V(f) on any Zariski neighborhood U of
all of X that preserves P exactly. Any affine-space retract
presentation of X would supply a retraction for this embedding by
lifting its coordinate functions and composing. Such a transferred
retraction need NOT preserve P, so nonexistence of unrestricted
retractions is not a conclusion.

The proof reduces U to D(h) with h=1 mod f. Units of A=B/(f) are
constants, so every irreducible factor of h restricts to a constant.
The target equation and exact preservation make r_x a unit after
inverting hP. Its restriction to X_P must then be a unit depending
only on z,t. This contradicts r_x|X_P=x because

    A_P=C[z,t,P^(-1)][x,x^(-1)].

This works with reducible P as well; no coprimality or primality of
x in A is assumed. It is a uniform argument, not a finite search.

finite-order solvability cannot obstruct the desired retraction.
This nu is not locally nilpotent; finite polynomial termination
cannot be silently inferred.

algebraizes the specified Taylor system, rather than some unrelated

### Accepted648: factorial closure does not transfer the action

Source: research/principal-retraction-birational-transfer-pass648-working.md.
For every integer g>=1 put F_g=x+y+x^(2g)*y^2 in B=C[x,y,z,t].
The map rho_g=(F_g,0,z,t) is a retraction with image
A_g=C[F_g,z,t], an actual polynomial three-ring, and kernel(y).
It is obtained from the ordinary hyperplane projection by the
polynomial extension G_g=(F_g,y,z,t) of the identity on y=0.

Every irreducible H(U,z,t) remains prime after U=F_g. The proof
passes to S=C[U,z,t]/(H) and uses the monic leading monomial
x^(2g)y^2 to give a free S-module quotient. Over Frac(S), the
y-discriminant has odd x-degree2g+1 for every U-class. Thus the
quotient is a domain. Unique factorization then makes A_g
factorially closed in B, not merely algebraically closed.

The geometric generic curve of rho_g has function field

    W^2=1-4x^(2g+1)+4U*x^(2g),

whose smooth projective model has genus g. It follows that NO
nonzero ambient LND annihilates A_g. Thus even principal kernel,
factorially closed polynomial image and transfer from an actual
trivial cylinder do not transfer an additive action to the chosen
retraction. G_g is etale along y=0 but has generic degree2g, and
is not a coordinate automorphism. The different ordinary projection
remains available, so the example is not an obstruction to choosing
some other successful retraction.

### A positive supplied-retraction test, with a published antecedent

For arbitrary domains A contained in B, a retraction rho with
ker(rho)=sB and s!=0 satisfies

    B=A[s] iff A is factorially closed in B
                 and Frac(B)=Frac(A)(s).

The proof has no UFD, normality, finiteness or characteristic
assumption. After localizing at A minus{0}, factorial closure
makes every unit constant over K=Frac(A). Inside K(s), Bezout
then eliminates denominators, giving the actual algebra K[s].
Repeated subtraction of rho(b) and division by s stays inside B
and terminates by polynomial degree, giving all coefficients in A.

With source coordinates a,v,tau, put

    u=1+av,    C=a-v*tau*u,    B=u-C,
    f_pq=-B^p-C^q: A3 -> A1.

The pair(B,C) never vanishes. Three explicit preimage formulas cover
every point of A2 minus0. Its row differential has rank two except
a=v=0, whose image is(1,0). At that locus partial_a(f_pq)=p, so f_pq
is everywhere smooth and surjective for allp,q>=2.

More strongly, its row-minor ideal is exactly J=(v^2,a+v*tau).
A written unimodular-row identity and differential wedge identities
put J inside the gradient ideal I. Modulo J the a-derivative equals

    p+v*(p*(2*(p-1)*tau-1)+4*tau*1_(q=2)),

a unit since v^2=0. Hence I=(1) uniformly in the exponents. This
is an exact ideal argument, not numerical evidence of nonvanishing.

Therefore f_23 x id_A2 is a smooth surjection A5 -> A3 with NO
rational section, even after further affine stabilization. Both
source and target are actual affine spaces. The dimensions match645;
no claim that their complete fiber families are identical is made.

### What the actual cylinder does supply

For an actual cylinder, i:X -> A4 and r:A4 -> X with r*i=id give
S(x,w)=r(i(x)+w). Its parameter differential is onto at w=0. They
also let every map Z -> X extend across every closed affine embedding
Z -> Y: extend the ambient coordinate functions and compose with r.
Conversely that extension property gives a retraction by applying it
to id_X in a closed affine embedding. This is a characterization of
affine-space retracts, not affine spaces, and not a section theorem
for smooth surjections. The comparator refutes the latter even for
a base possessing this entire extension property.

equivalent there; algebraic interpolation is different. For contractible
affine manifolds the latter is equivalent to being a regular retract.
No unsupported converse from strong dominability or a smooth cover
was used. The characteristic-zero [Riemann-Hurwitz formula](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0C1B)
was checked directly by root and both reviewers.

### Forcing a variable-time quotient does not supply local nilpotence

The diagonal-ideal criterion was already proved in23, Section2. General
located that exact duplicate; root reread Sections1--3 in c0ac26. The
additional attempted repair can be described completely. Let B=A[u],
E=partial_u, T an LND, and write

    T=D(u)+h(u) partial_u,
    delta_lambda=exp(lambda E) T exp(-lambda E),
    delta_lambda(lambda)=0.

The coefficients of D(u) are derivations of A. With w=u+lambda, the
ideal (w) is delta_lambda-stable precisely when h(0)=0. This means
Tu belongs to uB, and LND semivariance makes it equivalent to Tu=0.
Straightforward diagonal descent therefore cannot correct a coordinate
field which moves the chosen slice function.

One can force ideal stability by putting

    delta_tilde=delta_lambda-delta_lambda(u) partial_lambda.

In the polynomial presentation B[lambda]=A[w][u], this is exactly

    delta_tilde=D(w)+h(w) partial_u,    delta_tilde(w)=0.

Thus delta_tilde is LND if and only if D(w) is LND on A[w]. Necessity
is restriction; sufficiency follows from its action on A[w] and
delta_tilde^n(u)=D(w)^(n-1)(h(w)), then finite algebra generators.
No invariance assumption on h(w) under D(w) is needed. Renaming w as u
shows that this is exactly local nilpotence of the FULL horizontal part
T-T(u)E. This is stronger than checking the constant projected field.
The correction does not supply the missing condition by itself.

### A finite linear positive test with local nilpotence built in

Let B=C[X1,X2,X3,X4], E be the actual supplied LND with Eu=1,
and A=ker(E). Fix this actual coordinate order and a nonnegative
integer m. Use the ansatz

    T=sum t_i(X1,...,X_(i-1)) partial_Xi,  deg t_i <= m.

All unknowns are constant coefficients. Every such T, including every
linear combination in this ansatz, is locally nilpotent. Explicitly,
choose w1=1 and wi=1+m*max(wj:j<i). Each term strictly lowers this
positive monomial weight, so sufficiently many applications kill
every polynomial. No numerical nilpotence test is being substituted
for this proof.

The equations [T,E]=0 form a finite homogeneous linear system in
those unknowns. They make A stable under T, so its restriction is an
intrinsic LND. Under the SUPPLIED-pair assumptions of641, it is enough
that T(f) be nonzero to recognize A. The coefficient map T -> T(f)
is linear; success means its restriction to the commutator solution
space is nonzero. One may add the linear condition T(u)=0, but that
condition is not needed for this particular recognition implication.
No unit component of T is required either. These are positive
certificates, not a guarantee of success in any flag or finite bound.

Alternatively, with T(u)=0 and T(Xj)=1, the finite slice projection
q=sum (-u)^k E^k(Xj)/k! lies in A and satisfies T(q)=1. This gives
an actual intrinsic slice. The underlying recognition implications
are already retained in21,22 and641; they are not new theorems.
General independently reconstructed both criteria and the uniform
weight certificate. No permanent checker or new theorem note is added.

### Complete fixed-flag classification for the explicit643 control

Use the actual643 coordinates alpha,beta,gamma,U and set

    F=alpha gamma^2+beta gamma^3+gamma^5,  u=U-F,
    G=F_gamma=2 alpha gamma+3 beta gamma^2+5 gamma^4,
    E=(0,-alpha,-beta,1-alpha gamma^3-beta G).

Then Eu=1. Every strict triangular T in this displayed order
satisfying [T,E]=0 and T(u)=0 has exactly the form

    T(alpha)=0,
    T(beta)=alpha b(alpha),
    T(gamma)=b(alpha) beta+c(alpha),
    T(U)=alpha b(alpha) gamma^3+(b(alpha) beta+c(alpha))G,

with arbitrary polynomials b,c. To prove necessity, the beta
commutator forces T(alpha)=0. The gamma commutator then gives
T(beta)=alpha partial_beta T(gamma), forcing the displayed beta
and gamma components. The equation T(u)=0 determines T(U).
Conversely the commutator vanishes on alpha,beta,gamma,u, hence
on U=u+F as well. This proves sufficiency on the whole ring.

For nonzero T its total coefficient degree is exactly

    max(deg b+5, deg c+4),

omitting a zero polynomial. The monomials contributed by
5 b(alpha) beta gamma^4 and 5 c(alpha) gamma^4 cannot cancel
each other or the lower-gamma terms. Thus EVERY nonzero T in this
fixed-flag solution space has degree at least four. At bound m its
dimension is max(0,m-4)+max(0,m-3). At m=4 the unique direction is

    T=partial_gamma+G partial_U.

It has the intrinsic slice q=gamma+beta u+alpha u^2/2: Eq=0 and
Tq=1. This is a positive polynomial recombination repair of643's
fixed-line control. It is not a lower bound over different coordinate
orders or arbitrary nonlinear changes, and it is not a recognition
proof for an unknown cancellation candidate.

Jet deduplicated the zero constant-normalizer obstruction against

was created for that already retained result. A short refinement is:

      iff [delta,E]=0 and E(h)=0.

Indeed h delta is locally nilpotent, so the stable-base lemma21
makes normalization of the sliced E actual commutation. This makes
E preserve ker(delta). Since delta is sliced, the same lemma makes
[delta,E]=0; the bracket then forces E(h)=0. The converse is direct.
Thus invariant replicas of a failed constant coordinate direction
cannot repair normalization. This does not address nonlinear sums
or arbitrary new coordinate frames.

The separate evaluated-flow control is entirely on a known polynomial
base A=C[a1,a2,a3], B=A[u]. Set

    Xi=ai+u^(i+1),  i=1,2,3,
    W=u+X1^2+X2^2+X3^2.

The whole inverse is U=W-sum Xi^2, ai=Xi-U^(i+1), u=U. Every
constant ambient direction delta_c has projected infinitesimal
sum ci partial_ai. Nevertheless its flow, retracted to u=0, is

    ai -> ai+ci t-(t ell-t^2 k)^(i+1),
    ell=c4-2 sum ci ai,    k=sum ci^2  (i=1,2,3).

For the first generator the group-law defect, composition minus
the t+s map, has ts coefficient 2 ell^2. Vanishing forces all
four constants to be zero. Thus even commuting coordinate-LND
first derivatives do not make these evaluated ambient flows actions.
The projected infinitesimals themselves integrate perfectly well;
full evaluated-flow compatibility is an unnecessarily strong demand,
not a necessary condition for all intrinsic-action constructions.

The same chart has no nonzero constant normalizer of E=partial_u.
In ambient coordinates the first wedge minor of [delta_c,E] with E
is -6 U^2 delta_c(U), and delta_c(U)=c4-2 sum ci Xi.
The domain identity forces c=0. The replica lemma extends this
failure to nonzero invariant replicas of every constant direction.

### Accepted606: repair needs radical divisibility of DP, not of P

Let R=C[x_1,...,x_m], D be locally nilpotent, 0!=a in ker(D),
b the product of distinct irreducible factors of a, and P in R.
For E=aD+(1+DP)partial_t, the sufficient condition DP in bR gives
an explicit whole polynomial rectification, without homogeneity.
The hypothesis P in bR is unnecessary.

The evaluated base flows phi=Theta_P and eta=Theta_(-P) are inverse
modulo b because P becomes D-invariant there. Both fix a and b.
Their two compositions differ from the identity by operators raising
powers of b. If b^K belongs to aR, finite geometric sums invert both
compositions modulo a, and hence invert phi there. For

    Delta=phi eta-id,
    h=eta(sum_(j=0)^(K-1) (-Delta)^j(P)),
    W=P-at, Z_i=Theta_W(x_i), U=t+(h(Z)-P)/a,

the displayed division is exact, EZ_i=0 and EU=1. The localized
inverse is written in both directions. Modulo a, the base map is an
automorphism and U is affine in t with unit coefficient (1+DP)^(-1).
Injectivity modulo a then clears every denominator of the localized
inverse, including for nonprime a. Thus R[t]=C[Z_1,...,Z_m,U].

When a is nonconstant ordinary homogeneous and DP is zero or positive
ordinary homogeneous, the following are equivalent within this IMAGE
subclass: DP in bR; E has no zero; E has a polynomial slice; E is
polynomially rectified. The necessity proof itself works for arbitrary
positive homogeneous psi: a slice, or absence of zeros, for
aD+(1+psi)partial_t forces psi in bR. Sufficiency still requires psi=DP.
The nonhomogeneous-a and constant-DP controls show why those necessity
assumptions cannot be omitted. No arbitrary image-membership assertion
or general point-free-to-slice implication is made.

### Accepted601 and602: direct family reconstruction

601 treats f=xz-y^2, r=x^(2n+1)+y f^n and g=(f^(2n+1)+r^2)/x,
with H=Jac(f,g,.), d=4n,N=8n+2 and n>=1. For every q>=1 it proves

    R_(d+q) intersect ker H^(qN)
      = C H(z^q) direct-sum (R_(d+q) intersect ker H^(qN-1)).

The entire polynomial normal form, not a finite monomial sample, proves
the one-dimensional critical graded piece. With Y=y/z,V=f/z^2,
K=V^n+Y^(4n+1), the critical initial is a scalar multiple of Y^(4n)K.
The explicit correcting polynomial is c z^q/(qN). The actual last
coordinate degree strictly decreases and remains positive; no new-Euler
shift or arbitrary frame entry is asserted.

602 retains all coefficients F(x,f)=sum_(j=0)^n c_j x^(2n-2j) f^j,
c_0!=0. The actual determinant-one linear shear removing c_n preserves
f and all leading H-degrees. The monic key becomes

    K=V^n+sum_(j=0)^(n-1) c_j Y^(4n+1-4j) V^j.

The full tail has strictly larger valuation, and the correction is
c z^q/(qN c_0). The proof transports it back to the ORIGINAL z.
This is the whole ordinary-homogeneous DG family, not a classification
of all homogeneous rank-three LNDs.

Use the monomial base H_0 above, and put M=4n+1, s=M+1,
a=f^s, c=f g^2, H=aH_0 and psi=cH_0(z^q), n,q>=1.

(x+z,y+z,z,t) has degrees(N,N,N,qN) and exact first Euler shift.

deg_E(t-Q) below qN. The equation H^(qN)Q=H^(qN-1)psi isolates
the ordinary degree-q part. Its sole possible top contribution is
lambda z^q, requiring c=lambda a, contradicted by independence of f,g.

603 proves whole polynomial rectification by a finite general lemma:
for D LND, a,c invariant, a!=0 and c^K in aR, the extension
aD+(1+cDP)partial_t is rectifiable. With w=cP-at, set
Z=Theta_w(x), phi_0=Theta_(cP), Delta=phi_0-id and
h=sum_(j=0)^(K-1)(-Delta)^j(cP). Then

    U=t+(h(Z)-cP)/a

is polynomial, EU=1 and EZ=0. The geometric inverse modulo a is finite.
Its full last-coordinate coefficient is a unit even when a is nonprime.
The localized inverse and injectivity modulo a clear all denominators.
Both inverse directions are proved. Here c^s=a g^(2s), so the lemma
applies. A different actual frame(Z_1+U,Z_2+U,Z_3+U,U) has degrees1111.
Thus this is not a globally minimizing frame or a cancellation example.

It also gives the full omission-ring associated-graded criterion and

### Accepted605: arbitrary irreducible homogeneous base, with published inputs

Root's generalization no longer assumes the DG formulas. Let H be ANY
irreducible ordinary-homogeneous LND of C[x,y,z], d>0, with maximal
linear-coordinate H-degree N. For ell=d+q,k=qN-1, it proves the same
direct-sum equality as601 for all q>=1.

The proof identifies every external input, then verifies its hypotheses:

* Daigle2000 Facts1.6/1.7/1.9 and Lemma1.5 give homogeneous kernel
  generators of coprime degrees a,b and H=constant Jac(f,g,.), d=a+b-3.
* The generic affine orbit is K[r]. Its complete-intersection closure
  and birational polynomial parametrization give N=ab.
* The restricted projective valuation is centered at a closed point.
  A rational invariant h of ordinary degree1 identifies its field as
  C(w,s), with w=f^b/g^a, nu(s)=-1 and residue C(w). It is primitive
  divisorial, not a silently rescaled valuation.
* Every degree-e chart polynomial has nu<=eN; the two distinct
  irreducible dehomogenized f,g attain this bound. Thus muhat=N and
  the published unique-supraminimal-curve theorem forces minimality,
  hence final maximal contact value B=1/vol(nu)=N^2.
* The published plane Poincare formula H_gr=H_semigroup/(1-t^B)
  gives dimension at most one below B. The desired value dN+1 is
  strictly below N^2. The nonzero H(z^q) initial spans it.

The resulting actual shear lowers t's positive E-degree. It does NOT
place an arbitrary sliced four-variable derivation in those hypotheses,
or keep the next Euler shift fixed. Plane-valuation minimality is not
coordinate-frame degree minimality. These are explicitly distinguished.

### Accepted597: exact first shift without any polynomial slice

For n>=1 use a=2n+1,M=4n+1,N=8n+2 and the actual homogeneous base

    f=xz-y^2, r=x^a+yf^n, g=(f^a+r^2)/x,
    H=Jac(f,g,.), Hr=-gf^n,
    deg_H(x,y,z)=(2,4n+2,N), ordinary derivation degree(H)=4n.

Put ell=4n+2 and psi=H(z^2)+x^ell. Its exact H-degree is2N-1,
so s=deg_H(psi)+1=2N=N(ell-4n). The actual frame(x+z,y+z,z,t)
for E=H+(1+psi)partial_t has degrees(N,N,N,2N) and exact shift1.
The proof exhibits a polynomial invariant witnessing that exact shift.

Nevertheless psi is not in H(R)+ker H. Ordinary homogeneous degree
comparison reduces a putative primitive of x^ell modulo ker H to a
quadratic. Its required H-degree8n+5 is impossible: the six quadratic
monomial degrees are4,4n+4,8n+4,8n+4,12n+4,16n+4, with the last
two unique. This does not assume an unproved kernel classification.

The shear T=t-z^2 reduces E to H+(1+x^ell)partial_T. The source proves
that this extension has no polynomial slice of any degree. Two physical
points with y=T=0 and z=F/x are constructed over C[[F]] by a two-equation
formal implicit-function argument. At F=0 they have x2=epsilon*x1,
epsilon a primitive M-th root, equal g, and zero T-displacement.
The required coefficient is

    K=(epsilon^(a+1)-1)/((2ell+1)(epsilon^a-1)) != 0.

Choosing a nonzero root of1+K*x1^ell=0 gives a nonsingular two-variable
Jacobian, hence entire formal endpoints. They lie on the same actual
polynomial orbit with parameter tau=-(r2-r1)/(g F^n), of valuation-n.
A whole polynomial slice would have integral endpoint difference equal
to tau, a contradiction. The proof needs no algebraization or bounded
search. It is explicitly an UNSLICED control, not a cancellation example.

### Accepted598: the slice hypothesis does not repair the shortcut

Root and General independently found the same construction and
Laurent-residue obstruction. For the same homogeneous base and n>=2 put

    b=-g f^(n-2), psi0=fbr=-g f^(n-1)r,
    E0=H+(1+psi0)partial_T,
    v=fT-r^2/2, q=fbv-r,
    u0=T-brv+(fb^2/2)v^2.

Direct polynomial identities E0(v)=f,E0(q)=0 and f*u0=v+q^2/2
give E0(u0)=1. Now take

    psi=psi0+H(z^(4n)), E=H+(1+psi)partial_t,
    T=t-z^(4n), ell=8n, s=4nN.

The whole shear carries E0 to E and supplies an explicit polynomial
slice. Both summands in psi are ordinary homogeneous of degree8n;
their H-degrees are1 and4nN-1. Thus the actual frame(x+z,y+z,z,t)
has degrees(N,N,N,4nN), and its actual Euler field satisfies

    [E,D]=Nell partial_t-N(4n)E, [E,[E,D]]=0.

The invariant q after the shear has partial_t(q)=-f^n g, so
E(Dq)=-Nell f^n g !=0 and E^2(Dq)=0. This proves exact shift1
on the entire ring, not only the commutator upper bound.

For nonmembership, a decomposition psi0=H(Q)+K with HK=0 would force
H^2(Q)=g^2 f^(2n-1). The exact localization
R_fg=C[f,f^-1,g,g^-1,r], with H=-gf^n partial_r, gives

    Q=r^2/(2f)+A(f,g)r+B(f,g), A,B Laurent in f,g.

The prime quotient R_g/(f)=C[x,x^-1,y] has g=x^M and r=x^a.
Any higher pole in A,B would require cancellation between x-exponent
classes a and0 modulo M. At the simple pole, the nonzero quadratic
residue has class2a=1 modulo M, distinct from both. Thus Q cannot
be polynomial. Subtracting H(z^(4n)) proves the same obstruction for psi.

The source includes the exact extension of this argument to every
c in C[f,g], including zero:

    cr in H(R)+ker H  iff  f^n divides c  iff  cr in H(R).

Sufficiency uses H(-cx/(2f^n))=cr. Necessity uses the same three
residue classes at pole order n-ord_f(c). This is a specified-base
image test, not a classification of arbitrary extension slices.

These kernels are already recognized by595 at m=2,F(X,Z)=X^(2n).
Root reread that entire unchanged source in65fc3d+75c4c2; its hypotheses
m,n>=2,F(X,0) nonconstant and its slice match exactly. The whole shear
preserves kernel isomorphism and polynomial completion of the slice.
Thus598 refutes the image-plus-kernel bridge WITH sliceness, but neither
refutes cancellation nor claims an unknown quotient. No global minimality
of the displayed frame follows.

### Accepted599: selected-frame first shift can be supplied by a gauge

The follow-up passed complete saved-source review before acceptance.
Let H be a nonzero LND of R=C[x,y,z], homogeneous of ordinary derivation
degree d>0. Choose z of maximal H-degree N>=1. Let psi be ordinary
homogeneous of degree ell>d, q=ell-d>=1, and assume exactly

    deg_H(psi)<=qN-1.

Zero psi is allowed with degree convention minus infinity. For
E0=H+(1+psi)partial_T, the actual polynomial coordinates

    X=x+lambda z, Y=y+mu z, Z=z, t=T+gamma z^q

have E0-degrees(N,N,N,qN) for suitable complex constants, gamma nonzero.
Each base mixing excludes at most one value, including degree ties.
If qN>1, at most one extra gamma cancels the top H-coefficient;
if qN=1 the constant1 prevents vanishing even when all positive-degree
terms cancel, so no gamma exception is needed. The full polynomial
inverse is explicit. The new actual Euler field is

    D=N ordinaryEuler_R+qN t partial_t,
    [E,D]=Nell partial_t-NdE, [E,[E,D]]=0.

For k=qN-1, rho=H^(N-1)z,p=H^Nz, the whole polynomial

    B_h=sum(j=0..k) (-1)^j rho^(j+1) p^(k-j) H^j(h)/(j+1)!,
    h=1+psi+gamma H(z^q), I=p^(k+1)t-B_h

satisfies H(B_h)=p^(k+1)h,EI=0 and partial_t(I)=p^(k+1) !=0.
It witnesses exact shift1, without a global slice assumption. The
sum is valid also at k=0, and its proof is exact finite telescoping.

The gauge preserves sliceness, kernel isomorphism, and the coefficient
class modulo the vector subspace H(R)+ker H. Simultaneous conjugacy
of a pair(E,D) preserves shift. What changes here is the selected
coordinate frame and the Euler field recomputed from its new actual
degrees. In the explicit sliced control H=x^2(partial_y+partial_z),
psi=x^3y, the old degrees(1,1,1,2) have exact shift2, witnessed by
E0^2(D0 I0)=-x^9. The gauge t=T+z^3 yields degrees(1,1,1,3) and
exact shift1, witnessed by E(D1 I1)=4x^6. The degree sum increases
from5 to6. This is not a globally minimal-frame descent and does
not cover coefficients above the stated H-degree bound.

### Accepted600: direct rectification and a rank-three descended action

This separately reviewed addendum retains the entire595 recognition
proof and its actual whole polynomial automorphism Psi=Phi Gamma.
On B_f it observes

    E=partial_t+fL, L=H/f+br partial_t, A=-vL,
    [E,L]=[partial_t,L]=0, Ev=partial_t(v)=f,
    [E,A]=[partial_t,A]=-fL, [A,fL]=0.

Finite exponential commutation, with all signs checked, gives

    E Phi=Phi partial_t,
    partial_t Phi=Phi(partial_t-fL).

Gamma fixes t and commutes with partial_t, so E Psi=Psi partial_t
on the whole B. Therefore the actual polynomial coordinates
X=Psi(x),Y=Psi(y),Z=Psi(z),u=Psi(t) satisfy

    ker E=C[X,Y,Z], EX=EY=EZ=0, Eu=1.

The Taylor projection in595 remains valid; this extra computation
shows it acts identically on X,Y,Z. The old warning that Psi(t)=u
alone does not prove rectification remains correct. No change to595
or retraction of its proof is needed.

For every P in R, the original commuting partial_t satisfies

    partial_t Psi(P)=-Psi(Gamma^-1 H Gamma(P)).

Writing C(x) for the repair residue in595, Gamma^-1r=r+C f^(n-1).
Thus the conjugate base has

    Ftilde(X,Z)=F(X,Z)+(C(X)/X) Z^(n-1),
    rtilde=xFtilde(x,f)+y f^n,
    gtilde=(f^(mn+1)+rtilde^m)/x.

These are polynomial. The multiplier C/(xf) is delta0-invariant;
its replica has divergence zero, giving determinant Gamma=1 in
the localization. The complete Jacobian chain rule therefore gives
Gamma^-1 H Gamma=Jac(f,gtilde,.)=:Htilde. The full transformed
commuting derivation is

    Psi^-1 partial_t Psi
      =-Htilde+(1+gtilde f^(n-1)rtilde)partial_t.

The restriction to ker E, in its actual coordinates X,Y,Z, is
-Htilde. The [published DG Theorem5.7](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.00510v2)
applies exactly: m,n>=2 and Ftilde(X,0)=F(X,0) is nonconstant.

Rank three here is a published input with a verified parameter match,

recognition of that kernel, which is already polynomial. The598 gauge
fixes partial_t, so this conclusion transports to its first-shift examples.

### 595: uniform recognition for the specified Dasgupta--Gaifullin extensions

For m,n>=2 and F(x,0) nonconstant, put

    f=xz-y^m, R=xF(x,f), r=R+yf^n,
    g=(f^(mn+1)+r^m)/x, H=Jac(f,g,.),
    b=-gf^(n-2), E=H+(1+fbr)partial_t,
    v=ft-r^2/2, u=t-brv+(fb^2/2)v^2.

The source proves g polynomial and Hr=-gf^n, Hx=-mr^(m-1)f^n.
It also supplies direct local nilpotence: the base localized at fg
is C[f,f^-1,g,g^-1,r], with H=-gf^n partial_r. The exact expression
for z removes its apparent x denominator. Rank classification is
retained from the published DG base, not used as a substitute for
licensing the exponentials.

On B_f, L=H/f+br partial_t kills v, and Phi=exp(-vL) takes t to u.
Its x-image is the whole polynomial

    X=x+sum(j=1..m) binom(m,j) r^(m-j)g^(j-1)f^(j(n-1))v^j.

Let s=R(x,0). The y-image has at most a simple f-pole, with residue

    C=(m/2)s^(m+1)s' - s^(m+2)/(2x).

Because s is divisible by x, C/x is polynomial. The correction
Gamma=exp(-(C/(xf))(x partial_y+m y^(m-1)partial_z)) is therefore
an actual automorphism of B_f, not one requiring x to be inverted.
For Psi=Phi Gamma, the y-pole cancels and the relation
X Psi(z)=f+Psi(y)^m clears the z denominator in B.

The uniform finite-part proof retains both R(x,0) and [f]R, and
explicitly bounds every higher term. Only at n=2 do the second
Taylor term and the C'(x)(X-x)/f correction survive. All discarded
terms have f-order at least n+1; no F coefficient is silently set
to zero. The induced y-shift A(x,t) is divisible by x. Modulo f,

    x -> x, t -> t+P(x), y -> y+xQ(x,t),
    P=-s^(m+3)/(2x) for n=2, and P=0 for n>=3,
    Q=A/x.

The displayed cone-preserving z completion and its inverse are
polynomial on the whole ring. The same minimal-denominator lemma
then proves Psi^-1(B) is contained in B.

The finite Taylor homomorphism pi_E identifies B/(u) with ker E.
The three polynomials pi_E(Psi(x)), pi_E(Psi(y)), pi_E(Psi(z))
are algebraically independent generators of the kernel. They,
after adding u to each, together with u form an actual positive
frame of E-degrees(1,1,1,1) and Euler shift zero. In the concrete
592 member, this is strictly better than every affine frame.
It does not assert that Psi itself directly conjugates E to partial_t.
